metric: account-trie leaf count by depth level
source: 1× #5 geth inspect-trie (block 24,762,855); 3.5× PRISTINE scan (block 24,358,000); 5× #29 (block 24,546,596); 7× #35 (block 24,641,589); 10× #29 comment (block 24,759,769). Exact value-node counts per level.
note: Account-trie leaves by depth level. 1× and 3.5× nearly coincide (≈375M vs 392M accounts → same depth); 5×, 7×, 10× shift progressively deeper as account count grows (the peak walks from depth 9 → 10) — depth tracks log₁₆ of the account count. From 1× to 10× the median moves under one full level.

storageDepth.metric: storage-trie leaf count by depth level (aggregate over all contracts)
storageDepth.source: 1× nm StateComposition snapshot (block 24,927,663); 3.5× PRISTINE scan (block 24,358,000); 5× #29 (block 24,546,596); 7× #35 (block 24,641,589); 10× #29 (block 24,759,769). Value-node counts per level.
storageDepth.note: The opposite of account depth: mainnet storage tries are shallow (most leaves at depths 5–7, since most contracts hold 1–3 slots), but 3.5× → 10× pile up at depths 9–10 — the storage-spam mega-tries deepening each milestone (avg 7.24 → 7.81 from 5× to 10×). The per-contract histogram's open "16k+" bucket hides this; the depth distribution exposes it. (The x10 scan listed depths 6+ explicitly; the shallowest x10 levels are carried from x5/x7, where the upper storage trie is identical.)
